title: Design: Delete Customer window lists long dependent names inside the window
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer D, the payer, with no work orders, part sales, assets or contacts of its own, so only the Bill To rule can stop the delete.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, whose Bill Invoices To is saved as customer D, with a long name with spaces that no other customer has, at least 60 characters (for example Northern Plains Heavy Truck and Trailer Repair Services West).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, whose Bill Invoices To is saved as customer D, whose name is customer A's name with every space taken out (for example NorthernPlainsHeavyTruckandTrailerRepairServicesWest).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer C, whose Bill Invoices To is saved as customer D, with a name that no other customer has and that includes each of the characters & " ' < > (for example A&B "Fleet" O'Neil <Parts> & Sons).
  • If a name field stops before the end of a name, use the longest name it takes.
  • Open the attached picture bt-p6-05-after-delete-customer-refused.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
custom_steps:
1. Open customer D's Edit Customer window.
  2. Click Delete.
  3. Click Delete in the Confirmation window.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Customer D's Edit Customer window opens.

Step 2:

  • A "Confirmation" window asks "Are you sure you want to delete this company?" with "Cancel" and "Delete".

Step 3:

  • A "Delete Customer" window opens: "This customer is the default Bill To for [customer A's, customer B's and customer C's names, comma separated]. Remove it from those customers first."
  • Customer A, customer B and customer C are each listed as a link.
  • Every name stays inside the window: no part of it runs past the window's edge or covers the next name.
  • Customer C's name shows exactly as saved: the & " ' < > characters appear as typed, not changed into other characters or codes.
  • The "Cancel" and "Remove As Default Bill To" buttons are fully visible.

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as customer B's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Bill To", Confluence 1003585538, version 0.5 (6 Nov 2026, pending approval, Chris Ward), read 9 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-12289, story SV-12314 (Story 12, Deleting a customer that pays for others)

  • User Feedback Summary: “D8 | Delete a customer that is someone's default | "This customer is the default Bill To for [names, comma separated]. Remove it from [that customer / those customers] first." | "Delete Customer" window with links, "Cancel", "Remove As Default Bill To"”
  • S12-R2: “The window shows the refusal message and each dependent customer as a link to its page.”
  • S12-R3: “The window has "Cancel" and "Remove As Default Bill To" buttons.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Bill To design" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2prSHgwt2tWCz96QD2DWkd), version 1794510417-a68d (its boards are byte-identical to version 1794239066-4906 read 9 Nov 2026), read 13 Nov 2026: pictures "Delete Customer refused" (page 6 "Deleting a customer that pays for others", New, no before exists). Compare the screen with the pictures; the expected results come from the PRD.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • bt-p6-05-after-delete-customer-refused.png

The design's own words:

  • “Window "Delete Customer": "This customer is the default Bill To for Valders Diesel & Fleet Repair. Remove it from that customer first." Each dependent customer is a link.”

The design draws this place with ordinary names only; it draws no long name without spaces and no name with & " ' < >. The stress check follows the design-case checklist (lesson L-21); the expected words come from the PRD quotes above.
